Load and geometry checks

Ground forces are in newtons, not pressure. Holding force and moment are equal and opposite to the reported resultant; gravity is absent from this prescribed-pose experiment. Nodes share one ring energy. Refinement changes individual nodal forces, so compare total loads and energy across resolutions.

Author a ground profile

Ordered [x,z] points in metres with provenance, linear segments and solid below. Equal x values preserve a vertical face. Overhangs and layered response are not supported. Applying these points marks the profile as custom; terrain resolution controls only regenerate built-in examples.

What this establishes

A static radial displacement model can share load across several terrain regions. It has no tangential casing freedom, inflation, finite contact area, stress or traction law. Sharp corners and rim strikes can exceed this model: unsupported results carry no forces or deformed outline.

Next: explicit corner constraints, moving-wheel impacts, layered soil over roots/rock, tread contamination and sourced rim/spoke/bead failure with pressure loss. Whole-bike coupling, finite-width 3D lateral/turning loads and validated adaptive update rates remain future work.
